correctness.rationale: Parity makes n a square, the parameter prime is excluded from tau(n) by the quadratic nonresidue of -1, every other prime divisor of tau(n) forces exact multiplicative order 2 p^k, and the order-of-a-power formula bootstraps all exponents to divisibility by arbitrarily high powers of 2 p^k.

originality.rationale: The 2021 source leaves x^2-x+1 at a finite computation through 10^8 and the 2023 thesis still treats the type-II problem as unresolved. Searches found no theorem covering Phi_{2 p^k} for p congruent to 3 mod 4. Originality is to the best of our knowledge; an unspecified in-preparation article mentioned in the 2023 thesis is a material residual risk.

value.rationale: The theorem proves the previously computational x^2-x+1 case and places it in an infinite cyclotomic family of nonconstant type-II polynomials with exactly one relative tau-number, using a reusable multiplicative-order bootstrap.
